correctness.rationale: For the twelve lexicographically sorted cube edges of Q3, incidence yields a four-regular twelve-vertex line graph C with 24 edges. A selected vertex subset has all components of size at most two iff every selected vertex has <=1 selected neighbor, equivalently no connected triple among its vertices. Independent code enumerated all 4095 nonempty masks against the 56 forbidden triples: 455 faces, f-vector (12,66,164,177,36). There are exactly 1512 codimension-one cover relations. Applying the submitted pivot order (9,8,10,2,5,0,4,7,6,11,3,1) independently yielded 211 distinct cover pairs and exactly 33 critical faces (one vertex, thirty-two tetrahedra); the matching-pair SHA256 was dcb4b0037b4bb74d759593df4499029e78cdccf10b3f4ab342ab45790ce4e7d7, agreeing with source verification output. Orienting all 1512 covers upwards on the 211 matched pairs and downwards otherwise, an independent Kahn pass removed all 455 nodes, confirming an acyclic discrete-Morse matching. Forman then gives a CW model with one 0-cell and 32 3-cells, and no intermediate 1- or 2-cells; every 3-cell attaches to a point, so the integral homotopy is exactly wedge of thirty-two S^3. Independent mod-two ranks (11,55,109,36) check the face counts but are not used to infer the integral theorem. This is a complete finite enumeration for this fixed graph, not an unverified extrapolation.
residual_risks: Matching is a rigorous finite certificate only for this concrete graph, with labels and pivot order as stated.
The CW homotopy conclusion uses the standard discrete-Morse homotopy theorem; the finite F2 homology alone would not imply it.
No equivariant homotopy classification, homeomorphism, or all-hypercube theorem is proved.
